chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A deceased person whose head was cut off?” He said: “The diyah is upon him.” I said: “Then who takes his diyah?” He said: “The Imam. This belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And if his right hand or anything from his limbs is cut off, then the arsh is upon him for the Imam.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money or prescribed financial compensation
key_terms.الْأَرْشُ: assessed indemnity for bodily injury less than full diyah
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, who receives this compensation in this ruling
key_terms.يَمِينُهُ: his right hand, mentioned as an example of a severed limb

ai.seo_question: Who receives the compensation for mutilating a deceased person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning mutilation of a deceased person. It states that financial liability is due for severing the head or limbs of the dead, and that this compensation is received by the Imam, since the right involved is ascribed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5358 - It is narrated from Abu Jamilah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a deceased person whose head was cut off.
Imam (as) said: "The blood money is upon the one who did it."
I asked: "Who receives his blood money?"
Imam (as) said: "The Imam, for this belongs to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. And if his right hand or any of his limbs is cut off, the compensation (Al-arsh) is also due to the Imam."
